title: South Carolina AI Laws

reading.body:
South Carolina's only AI-related law is a ceremonial resolution declaring March 30 to April 2, 2026, as AI Week, not a binding rule.

The pattern here is absence. A state that has passed one AI law has passed a commemoration, which encourages citizens to learn about artificial intelligence and imposes nothing on anyone. There is no covered entity, no effective date with obligations attached, and no requirement to read.

For AI specifically, this matters because the binding constraints on data centers are not only statutes. They are interconnection queues, power procurement, water permits, and local zoning, none of which appear in this data. A state can be a significant site of AI buildout while its enacted AI law consists of a week on the calendar.

What this does not tell the reader is anything about South Carolina's actual posture toward AI. It does not cover pending bills, executive orders, utility regulation, or local ordinances. It covers one enrolled law, and that law is a resolution.

How this page is kept
